deck.noPictures: The subject is private company economics, model performance and financing; photographs would not substantiate the comparative claims.
deck.brief: Investor and strategy pre-read. Compare Anthropic and OpenAI by near-term demand, frontier capability, distribution and capital access, then state conditional long-term scenarios. Evidence cut: 27 September 2026. Company run rates and financing announcements are unaudited and basis-specific.
deck.question: Who is better positioned in the short run and long run, and which company has the stronger capital structure?
deck.answer: OpenAI leads direct consumer reach and disclosed funding access; Anthropic leads selected paid enterprise signals and the latest measured premium-model benchmark. Neither has a provably superior overall capital structure or a defensible long-run win on public evidence.

settles.what: current segment leadership and long-run uncertainty

pages.title: OpenAI owns reach; Anthropic leads selected enterprise signals; neither owns the future

points.text: OpenAI has more than one billion weekly ChatGPT users and 57% of August visits to six major chatbot sites. That is a large direct funnel into subscriptions, ads and workplace sales. No matched Claude weekly-user or paid-conversion series is public, so this is a reach lead rather than a profit verdict.

Anthropic passed OpenAI in Ramp’s US purchase-incidence panel by May and led 43.8% to 39.8% in August. It also reported more than 500 accounts above $1 million annualized spend. Buyers may pay both firms, and matched retention or contribution is unpublished; the enterprise lead is deliberately narrow.

Opus 5.5 scores highest among five selected models on one current Artificial Analysis index. GPT-6 Astra matches Fable 5.1 quality there at lower estimated task cost. Earlier coding-agent tests use another denominator. Customer tasks at matched effort and dollars per successful outcome remain the practical test.

OpenAI disclosed $122 billion committed financing and a confirmed undrawn revolver; Anthropic announced a $65 billion round at a higher, later private mark. Comparable funded cash, burn and timed obligations are absent. Today’s signals split by segment, while long-run economic leadership and overall capital quality remain unranked until contribution and cash coverage are observed.

pages.source: Sources: OpenAI reach and funding, 2026; Anthropic Series G/H, 2026; Ramp AI Index, Sep 2026; Similarweb, Sep 2026; Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2.

points.text: Ramp’s adoption rates overlap because enterprise buyers often use multiple models. A lead in payment incidence does not imply exclusive deployment, and one large account can drive more spend than many small purchasers.

pages.title: Headline run rates cannot settle the revenue race without channel accounting

blocks.label: Gross versus net
points: Axios reports Anthropic includes full sales through some cloud channels while OpenAI recognizes only its share of some partner sales.
The same downstream sale can therefore create different reported run-rate amounts. A buyer can spend the same amount while the two labs show different headline revenue.

blocks.label: Run rate versus booked
points: Annualized snapshots extrapolate recent activity and can jump with contracts or channel timing.

They are not the same as twelve months of recognized, audited revenue. A change in recent usage or annualization window can shift the displayed level even without a comparable change in contracted value.

blocks.label: Revenue versus value
points: Neither company publishes comparable segment gross margins or net cash flow.

High top-line growth may require heavy inference, training and customer acquisition spending. Compute contracts can turn impressive revenue growth into a weak cash return if utilization or pricing disappoints.

pages.source: Sources: Axios, revenue accounting (Sep 2026); Anthropic, Series H (May 2026); OpenAI, financing release (Mar 2026).

pages.title: OpenAI already has a second monetization engine in advertising

items.label: time from launch to stated milestone

points: OpenAI said ChatGPT Ads passed a one-billion-dollar annualized revenue run rate within 200 days of launch and opened direct Ads Manager buying across additional markets. The result provides a monetization route that Anthropic has not publicly matched and could support lower-priced consumer access.

Annualized ad run rate is not full-year recognized revenue, profit or evidence of user satisfaction. Advertising could also change trust and product use, so its strategic value depends on durable engagement and advertiser returns after the launch period. Sustained advertiser demand and user retention after wider rollout are the tests that make this route strategically material.

exhibit.caption: The x-axis is hypothetical volume growth after the observed market price fall; the y-axis is a modeled index, not company revenue.

pages.rail: Ramp’s observed token price fell from $1.15 to $0.68. At unchanged mix, paid volume must rise about 69% to restore starting revenue. The plotted cases are assumptions; serving cost and partner take decide whether cash contribution improves.

settles.what: illustrative $100-sale contribution under two partner takes

pages.title: Partner take shifts the break-even serving-cost boundary
pages.source: Analyst $100-sale sensitivity; 15% and 45% partner takes are assumptions, not company contract rates.

exhibit.heading: Contribution after channel and serving costs

points: At a 45% partner take, $55 of serving cost consumes the remaining sale value; contribution turns negative above that cost. At a 15% take, the break-even serving cost is $85.

The two partner takes and serving costs are analyst assumptions on one $100 customer sale. Actual OpenAI and Anthropic channel terms, product mix, fixed costs and accounting judgments are undisclosed.

The two slopes differ by exactly $30 at every serving-cost level because the assumed partner take differs by 30 percentage points. That fixed gap can change which product or channel is worth scaling even when both report the same end-customer sale.

points.text: OpenAI leads direct reach; Anthropic leads selected paid enterprise panels and the latest measured premium-model score. These are different signals, so neither ranks overall task economics.

A lasting lead requires retained paid tasks at positive contribution and cash coverage of compute obligations. Neither firm discloses these measures on a matched basis; the outcome can remain unresolved beyond 2030.
Call a single leader only if it clears the task and cash tests while leading both direct and enterprise demand. Reassess as comparable paid cohorts, margins and funded liquidity become public.

points: A single model score or funding mark cannot clear all four tests. Demand and margins must be observed together on the same quarter and accounting basis.

points: At half OpenAI’s contribution per successful task, Anthropic would need more than 66.7% of the two firms’ paid tasks to generate more segment contribution. At equal contribution, the hurdle is 50%; at double contribution, it falls to 33.3%.

This is an analyst sensitivity for a two-provider segment with positive contribution per task; it is not observed market share or a company forecast. The overall verdict still requires both segments and funded cash coverage.

points: The same transaction can reward a consumer or workplace application, a model provider and its cloud supplier. ChatGPT’s reach supports the application route, while Anthropic’s Ramp adoption supports a model procurement route; neither signal states the value split.

Actual application fees, cloud costs, direct-channel take and task-level contribution are private. A winner in usage can therefore capture less economic value than a partner. The flow is a structure, not a $100 allocation or forecast.

settles.what: final answer and monitoring decision

pages.title: Short-run signals split; the long-run economic leader is unranked
items: Short run, 12–24 months: OpenAI is better placed for mass-market attention and broad distribution, anchored by more than one billion weekly ChatGPT users. Anthropic has stronger evidence of premium enterprise adoption in selected payment and spend measures, plus the latest independent frontier-quality lead.

Capital: OpenAI has the larger disclosed 2026 financing commitment and a confirmed undrawn credit facility. Anthropic has the higher latest private mark. Neither publishes the comparable balance sheets and cash economics needed to name an overall stronger capital structure.

Long run, three to seven years: no defensible single economic winner today. Anthropic’s route is sustained premium task quality and enterprise retention at attractive contribution. OpenAI’s route is converting its large audience and broad product surface into low-cost, habitual work. A split economic outcome would require both firms to earn positive contribution with adequate cash coverage in the segments they lead.

Revisit the verdict quarterly using matched task outcomes, cost per successful task, paid cohort retention, delivered compute and audited cash margins. Funding rounds and launch benchmarks matter only insofar as they improve those measures.
